![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

The file read operation for `provision-golden.sh` (and other files read dynamically in this block) is performed using the `read` helper, which directly calls `fs.readFileSync` without error handling.

If any of these files are missing or unreadable, the script will throw an unhandled exception and crash, preventing the generation of stable, typed JSON failure diagnostics (e.g., the structured `errors` array in the JSON output).

Additionally, `scripts/infra/windows-hyperv-runner/golden-image/provision-golden.sh`, `scripts/infra/windows-hyperv-runner/golden-image/cie-runner-bootstrap.sh`, and `scripts/infra/windows-hyperv-runner/golden-image/cie-runner-bootstrap.service` are not included in the `requiredFiles` array, meaning their existence is not pre-validated.

### Recommendation
1. Add these files to the `requiredFiles` array so they are explicitly checked for existence.
2. Update the `read` helper function to wrap `fs.readFileSync` in a `try-catch` block, appending any read errors to the `errors` array and returning an empty string, ensuring the script fails closed with stable, typed diagnostics.

<details>
<summary>References</summary>

1. When performing file reads or external inspections (such as PDF parsing), wrap the operations in try-catch blocks to catch errors and convert them into stable, typed failure diagnostics with a nonzero fail-closed exit code.
</details>

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Allow JIT config writes before starting the runner**

When this service starts a real `run.sh --jitconfig` runner, refreshing `run-helper.sh` is only the first root write: in actions/runner v2.335.1, `Runner.Listener` decodes the JIT config and writes each config entry under the runner root with `File.WriteAllBytes` before `LoadSettings`, which creates files such as `.runner` and credentials in `/opt/actions-runner`. With `ProtectSystem=strict` and `ReadWritePaths` limited to `run-helper.sh`, `_diag`, and `_work`, those root-level config writes still fail read-only, so the runner remains offline even after this remediation.
